deities: Goddess Jwala Devi / Jwalamukhi (worshipped as eternal flames, no idol)
Nine flames named for Mahakali, Annapurna, Chandi, Hinglaj, Vindhya Vasini, Mahalakshmi, Saraswati, Ambika and Anji Devi (forms of the Goddess)

history.dynasty: Initial shrine attributed to King Bhumi Chandra (Katoch); present structure Dogra-period; legendary Pandava renovation
history.period: Antiquity legendary ('first temple built by the Pandavas' per folklore); present form attributed to the Dogra period
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 372 / 'Jwala Ji Temple' (Jawalamukhi) - same temple. Jwala Ji is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas: Sati's tongue is believed to have fallen here, and the goddess manifests as natural eternal flames burning from fissures in the rock (science attributes them to natural-gas seepage; a 1970s government exploration reportedly found no reservoir - verify). There is no idol - the nine jyotis (flames), named for forms of Durga, are the deity. Legend says a cowherd discovered the flames, King Bhumi Chandra built the first shrine after following the trail, and the Pandavas later renovated it. Emperor Akbar, skeptical, tried to douse the flames with water and an iron disk; failing, he humbly offered a golden canopy/parasol (which legends say changed its composition). Rabdi is the customary offering, and five aartis are held daily. The temple is built in Nagara/Shikhara style with Pahari and Dogra-period elements.

name: Jwala Ji Temple
town: Jwalamukhi (CSV town correct; also spelled Jawalamukhi)
town_description: Jwalamukhi is a temple town in Kangra district, Himachal Pradesh, set in the lap of the Shivalik range (the Kalidhar) about 30-35 km south of Kangra town. It is one of the most important pilgrimage towns in Himachal Pradesh, anchoring the Kangra Valley's Shakti circuit alongside Chintpurni, Bajreshwari and Chamunda Devi. The town takes its name from the 'flaming mouth' (jwala-mukhi) of the goddess.

travel.railway: Jwalamukhi Road station - about 20 km (verify); Pathankot Junction is the nearest major railhead, about 120 km (verify).
travel.road: Well connected by road to Kangra (~30 km), Dharamshala, Chandigarh and Pathankot by buses and taxis (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: March to June and September to November for pleasant weather; Navratri fairs (March-April, September-October) are the grandest but crowded.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): goldentriangletour lists summer 5:00 AM-10:00 PM, winter 6:00 AM-9:00 PM with four/five aartis (Mangal, Bhog, Sandhya, Shayan); inheritage.foundation lists 6:00 AM-9:00 PM daily.
